sentences.text: 4  MFA No. 200077 of 2023  THIS MFA IS FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF THE MOTOR VEHICLES ACT, PRAYING TO SET ASIDE THE IMPUGNED JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 20.01.2022 PASSED IN M.V.C. NO.771 OF 2020 BY THE PRINCIPAL SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND MACT-V AT VIJAYAPURA.

THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
Though these matters are listed for admission, with consent of learned counsel for parties, they are taken-up for final disposal.

2. Challenging common judgment and separate awards dated 20.01.2022, passed by Principal Senior Civil Judge and MACT-V, at Vijaypura, (for short 'tribunal') in MVC.no.772/2020 and MVC.no.771/2020, these appeals are filed.
3. MFA.no.200736/2022 and MFA.no.200894/2022 are filed by claimants, MFA.no.202872/2022 and MFA.no.200077/2023 are filed by owner.
4. Shri Sunilkumar P. Bangari, learned counsel for owner submitted that appeals were filed challenging dismissal of claim petition against respondent no.2 - insurer and exoneration of its liability.
It was submitted that only reason assigned by tribunal for dismissal of claim petition against insurer was that at time of accident, insured vehicle did not have fitness certificate.
It was submitted that at time of recording evidence, owner had misplaced fitness certificate and was therefore unable to produce same before tribunal.
It was submitted that vehicle was inspected on 22.05.2019 and issued fitness certificate valid upto 21.05.2021.
Copy of said certificate was produced as additional evidence along with I.A.no.1/2022 filed under Order XLI Rule 27 of CPC.
In view of same, dismissal of claim petition against insurer and its exoneration from liability would be illegal and sought for modifying award.

6. It was submitted that due to certificate having been misplaced, despite due diligence, fitness certificate could not be produced before tribunal and since same was required for proper disposal of appeal, he sought for allowing I.A.no.1/2022.
It was further submitted that this Court by order dated 21.06.2023, had permitted insurer to ascertain genuinity and authenticity of fitness certificate.
In view of non-filing of objections to I.A.no.1/2022, application requires consideration.

Ramesh S/O Shivappa Guled vs Shivappa And Anr on 14 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102761995/
5 7.

entities.text: Shivappa Guled vs Shivappa And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Shri Uday P. Honguntikar, learned counsel for respondent no.2-insurer fairly submitted that fitness certificate produced by owner along with I.A.no.1/2022 was genuine.

In view of same,
insurer would not contest appeal on this aspect.

But, insofar as finding of tribunal on contributory negligence between rider of motorcycle and driver of Lorry, it was submitted that as on date of accident rider of motorcycle did not have driving licence.
Therefore, instead of apportionment of 50% against rider of motorcycle and driver of Lorry, entire negligence was required to be held against rider of motorcycle.
8. Insofar as quantum of compensation, it was submitted that as on date of accident, notional income for year 2020 was Rs.13,750/-.

But, tribunal considered monthly income as Rs.14,750/-
which was excessive.
It was further submitted that even award under other heads were excessive and sought for set-off against claimant's appeal for enhancement.
Shri Bapugouda Siddappa, learned counsel for claimants submitted that appeals were filed for enhancement of compensation.
It was submitted that they were also challenging finding of tribunal on contributory negligence as it had denied 50% of compensation assessed to claimants.
It was submitted that accident in question occurred solely on account of rash and negligent driving of Lorry by its driver.
As per Ex.P7 - accident spot sketch, accident occurred on Athani-Vijayapura road running east to west.
Motorcycle was proceeding from west to east on a road 28 feet in width, with 5 feet kacha road on each side.
Accident spot was at 12 feet from northern edge of road.

Therefore,
Lorry driver was driving it on his wrong side at accident spot.
It was further submitted that entire criminal prosecution records implicated only Lorry driver alone.
Therefore, regardless of whether rider of motorcycle possessed driving licence to drive motorcycle, above material would establish that accident occurred due to sole negligence of Lorry driver.
Hence, apportionment of negligence at 50% each was not justified.

10. Insofar as appeal for enhancement, it was submitted that in MVC.no.772/2020, claimant - Shivappa, aged 45 years was working as mason and earning Rs.18,000/- per month sustained comminuted displaced fracture of nasal bone and proximal end of right tibia with intra-articular extension with ipsi lateral inter-trochantric fracture.
Same was assessed by PW-3 to have caused permanent disability to extent of 35-40% to right lower limb.
However, tribunal considered monthly income at only Rs.14,750/- and disability at 13% awarded inadequate compensation.
It was submitted that even award under other heads namely, pain and suffering, loss of income during laid-up period and loss of amenities was on lower side and sought enhancement.
11. Insofar as MVC.no.771/2020, claimant - Nimbevva, aged 37 years working as coolie and earning Rs.15,000/- per month sustained fracture of mid-shaft of femur and neck of right femur.

Same was assessed by - 10 - Ramesh S/O Shivappa Guled vs Shivappa And Anr on 14 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102761995/
6 NC: 2023:KHC-K:6439 PW-3 to have caused 30-35% disability to right limb.

entities.text: Shivappa Guled vs Shivappa And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But, tribunal considered her monthly income as only Rs.14,750/-, disability at 11% and awarded inadequate compensation.
It was submitted that even award under other heads namely, pain and suffering, loss of income during laid-up period and loss of amenities was on lower side and sought enhancement.
On above grounds sought for allowing claimants' appeal.

12. Heard learned counsel, perused impugned judgment and awards and also certified copies of pleadings, deposition and exhibits made available at time of hearing.
13.

From above submission, it is seen that owner of Lorry is in appeal challenging exoneration of liability of insurer; while claimants are questioning apportionment of negligence against rider of motorcycle and denial of compensation to said extent.
Insurer while accepting liability is contending excessive award and seeks for set- off against enhancement.

Therefore, points that would arise for consideration are:
- 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:6439 i.
Whether I.A.no.1/2022 filed under Order XLI Rule 27 of CPC for additional evidence deserves to be allowed?
And if so, whether dismissal of claim petition against insurer and fastening liability on owner calls for modification?
ii. Whether apportionment of contributory negligence between rider of motorcycle and driver of Lorry, calls for interference?
iii. Whether claimants are entitled for enhancement of compensation?

Point no.(i):
14.

On perusal of impugned award, it is seen that only reason on which tribunal has exonerated insurer and held owner liable to pay compensation is that as on date of accident, insured vehicle (Lorry) was not issued with fitness certificate.
Accident occurred on 22.06.2020.
Certified copy of fitness certificate is produced by owner along with I.A.no.1/2022 filed under Order XLI Rule 27 of CPC.
Existence of fitness certificate would go to root of matter insofar as liability of insurer.

Further,
learned counsel for insurer has got fitness certificate verified as genuine and based on instructions fairly conceded that - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:6439 dismissal of claim petition on ground of non-production of fitness certificate as unsustainable.
15. On perusal of fitness certificate, it is seen that it was issued to insured vehicle on 22.05.2019 till expiry on 21.05.2021.
Said period would cover date of accident.
Hence, it is held that I.A.no.1/2022 deserves to be allowed and dismissal of claim petition against insurer requires to be set-aside.
Consequently, point no.(i) is answered in affirmative as above.

Ramesh S/O Shivappa Guled vs Shivappa And Anr on 14 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102761995/
7 Point no.(ii):
16.

entities.text: Shivappa Guled vs Shivappa And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In order to establish occurrence of accident due to negligence of driver of Lorry,
claimants had produced FIR, Complaint, Panchnama, Rough Sketch, Motor Vehicle Inspectors Report and Charge sheet as Exhibits-P1 to P3 and P7 to P9 respectively.
FIR/Complaint reveal that complaint is filed by Jyoti - daughter-in-law of claimant in MVC.no.772/2020.
Said complaint is filed against driver and owner of Lorry.
Police after investigation filed charge-sheet (Ex.P9) against rider of motorcycle as well as driver of Lorry.
While passing impugned award tribunal - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:6439 considered charge-sheet and based only on same, apportioned negligence against rider of motorcycle and driver of Lorry equally.
17. But contents of Ex.P7-accident spot sketch would reveal that accident occurred on 28 feet wide road running east to west.
Motorcycle was moving from west to east, while Lorry was coming from opposite direction.
Accident spot is at distance of 12 feet from northern edge of road.
This would establish that Lorry had gone on wrong side and dashed against motorcycle.
Considering fact that Lorry being heavy vehicle, duty of its driver to take care of other road users would be more.
And place of occurrence of accident would establish negligence on part of Lorry driver.
Considering above facts and circumstances, it would be appropriate to apportion negligence against rider of motorcycle at 25% and 75% against Lorry driver.
18. However, it is seen that owner of motorcycle himself was rider and is claimant in MVC.no.772/2020.
While in MVC.no.771/2020, it is by third party.

Therefore, it is held that insurer would be liable to pay entire - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:6439 compensation to third party claimant in MVC.no.771/2020 and thereafter recover 25% of compensation from Owner/rider of Motorcycle.
In MVC.no.772/2020, there would be denial of compensation to extent of 25% to claimant in MVC.no.772/2020.
Point no.(ii) is answered partly in affirmative as above.

Point no.(iii):
19.

Though it was stated that claimant aged 45 years was earning Rs.18,000/-
per month from mason work, there was no specific evidence to substantiate same.

In absence,
tribunal assessed it notionally at Rs.14,750/- which is questioned by insurer as being excessive.
Since notional income for year 2020, adopted for settlement of cases before Lok Adalath is Rs.13,750/-, same has to be considered.

8 20.

entities.text: Shivappa Guled vs Shivappa And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Insofar as loss of earning capacity, from Exs.P5 and P6 - wound certificate and discharge summary as well as Ex.P21 - disability certificate, claimant sustained comminuted displaced fracture of nasal bone and proximal end of right tibia with intra-articular extension with ipsi - 15 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:6439 lateral inter-trochantric fracture, assessed by PW-3 to have resulted in functional disability of 35-40% to right lower limb.

On ground that PW-3 had not treated claimant,
tribunal disbelieved his assessment and considered disability at 13%.
Merely on ground that doctor examined by claimant had not administered treatment would not bar him from assessing disability.
Ex.P21 discloses that PW-3 is an Orthopaedic Surgeon.
During clinical examination restriction of movement of knee due to mal-union of fractures with implants in situ is noted.
It is also observed that claimant was walking with limp on right side.

Considering occupation of claimant as mason,
restriction of movements of lower limb would definitely affect earning capacity to a higher extent.
Hence, assessment of functional disability of 13% would be inadequate.
Under above facts and circumstances, it would be appropriate to consider it at 17.5%.

Thus future loss of income would be:
Rs.13,750/- X 17.5% X 12 X 14 = Rs.4,04,250/-.
21.

Even when claimant sustained several fractures, tribunal awarded only Rs.20,000/- towards pain and - 16 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:6439 suffering which would be on lower side and therefore enhanced to Rs.40,000/-.
Taking note of period of inpatient treatment at 22 days and amount for which medical bills were produced, tribunal awarded Rs.3,32,000/-.
Same appears just and proper and therefore not interfered with.
Normally fractures take three months time to heal.
Considering said period as lay- off, claimant would be entitled for Rs.41,250/-.
Further, taking note of number of fractures and disability assessed, award of Rs.10,000/- towards loss of amenities would be inadequate and is enhanced to Rs.25,000/-.
Thus, total compensation would be Rs.8,42,500/-.
Point no.(iii) in MVC.no.772/2020 is answered partly in affirmative.

Though it was stated that claimant aged 37 years was earning Rs.15,000/-
per month from coolie work, there was no specific evidence to substantiate same.

In absence,
tribunal assessed it notionally at Rs.14,750/- which is questioned by insurer as being excessive.

Since notional income for year 2020,
- 17 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:6439 adopted for settlement of cases before Lok Adalath is Rs.13,750/-, same has to be considered.

9 23.

sentences.text: Insofar as loss of earning capacity, from Exs.P16 and P17-wound certificate and discharge summary as well as Ex.P22-disability certificate, claimant sustained fracture of mid-shaft of femur and neck of right femur.
Same was assessed by PW-3 to have caused 30-35% disability to right limb.
On ground that PW-3 had not treated claimant, tribunal disbelieved his assessment and considered disability at 11%.
Merely on ground that doctor examined by claimant had not administered treatment would not bar him from assessing disability.
Ex.P22 discloses that PW-3 is an Orthopaedic Surgeon.
During clinical examination restriction of movement of knee due to mal-union of fractures is noted.
It is also observed that there was shortening of right lower limb by two centimeters.
Inability to sit cross-legged or squat for long duration was also noted.
Considering occupation of claimant as coolie, above restrictions would affect earning capacity.

Hence,
assessment of functional disability of only - 18 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:6439 11% would be inadequate and is enhanced to 17.5%.

Thus future loss of income would be:
Rs.13,750/- X 17.5% X 12 X 15 = Rs.4,33,125/-.
24.
Claimant herein sustained grievous fracture to her right femur.
But tribunal awarded only Rs.20,000/- towards pain and suffering which would be on lower side and therefore enhanced to Rs.50,000/-.
Taking note of period of inpatient treatment at 8 days and amount for which medical bills were produced, tribunal awarded Rs.1,11,730/-.
Same appears just and proper and therefore not interfered with.
Normally fractures take three months time to heal.
Considering said period as lay- off, claimant would be entitled for Rs.41,250/-.
Further, taking note of number of fractures and disability assessed, award of Rs.10,000/- towards loss of amenities would be inadequate.
If same is enhanced to Rs.50,000/- it would be just and proper.
Thus, total compensation would be Rs.6,86,105/-.
Point no.(iii) in MVC.no.771/2020 is answered partly in affirmative.

25. In view of above findings, I pass following:
- 19 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:6439 ORDER i.
is allowed in part.
Compensation is reassessed to Rs.8,42,500/-.
But claimant would be entitled to only 75% of same with interest at 6% per annum from date of claim petition till deposit.
ii. MFA.no.200894/2022 is allowed in part.
Claimant is held entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.6,86,105/- with interest at 6% per annum from date of claim petition till deposit.
iii. MFA.no.200077/2023 is allowed.

sentences.text: 10 Statutory amount deposited is ordered to be refunded to appellant.
iv. MFA.no.202872/2022 is allowed, but amount in deposit is ordered to be transmitted to tribunal for payment to claimant or adjustment against liability of insurer.
v. Apportionment of negligence between rider of motorcycle would be at 25% and against driver of Lorry at 75%.

But insurer would be liable to pay entire compensation to claimant in - 20 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:6439 MFA.no.200894/2022 (MVC.no.771/2020) in first instance and thereafter recover 25% from rider/owner of motorcycle.
 vi. Insurer is held liable to pay  compensation to claimants in manner  indicated herein.
It is directed to deposit compensation before tribunal within period of six weeks from date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
vii. On deposit, 40% is ordered to be kept in fixed deposit and remaining 60% is ordered to be released to claimants on proper identification.
In view of disposal of main appeals, pending applications are disposed of as unnecessary.

 JUDGMENT
Though these matters are listed for admission, with consent of learned counsel for parties, they are taken-up for final disposal.
2. Challenging common judgment and separate awards dated 20.01.2022, passed by Principal Senior Civil Judge and MACT-V, at Vijaypura, (for short 'tribunal') in MVC.no.772/2020 and MVC.no.771/2020, these appeals are filed.
opennyai_summary.facts:
It was submitted that only reason assigned by tribunal for dismissal of claim petition against insurer was that at time of accident, insured vehicle did not have fitness certificate.
It was submitted that at time of recording evidence, owner had misplaced fitness certificate and was therefore unable to produce same before tribunal.
It was submitted that vehicle was inspected on 22.05.2019 and issued fitness certificate valid upto 21.05.2021.
Copy of said certificate was produced as additional evidence along with I.A.no.1/2022 filed under Order XLI Rule 27 of CPC.
In view of same, dismissal of claim petition against insurer and its exoneration from liability would be illegal and sought for modifying award.
6. It was submitted that due to certificate having been misplaced, despite due diligence, fitness certificate could not be produced before tribunal and since same was required for proper disposal of appeal, he sought for allowing I.A.no.1/2022.
It was further submitted that this Court by order dated 21.06.2023, had permitted insurer to ascertain genuinity and authenticity of fitness certificate.
NC: 2023:KHC-K:6439
Ramesh S/O Shivappa Guled vs Shivappa And Anr on 14 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102761995/
5 7.
But, insofar as finding of tribunal on contributory negligence between rider of motorcycle and driver of Lorry, it was submitted that as on date of accident rider of motorcycle did not have driving licence.
Therefore, instead of apportionment of 50% against rider of motorcycle and driver of Lorry, entire negligence was required to be held against rider of motorcycle.
However, tribunal considered monthly income at only Rs.14,750/- and disability at 13% awarded inadequate compensation.
It was submitted that even award under other heads namely, pain and suffering, loss of income during laid-up period and loss of amenities was on lower side and sought enhancement.
On above grounds sought for allowing claimants' appeal.
From above submission, it is seen that owner of Lorry is in appeal challenging exoneration of liability of insurer; while claimants are questioning apportionment of negligence against rider of motorcycle and denial of compensation to said extent.
opennyai_summary.arguments: Insurer while accepting liability is contending excessive award and seeks for set- off against enhancement.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Therefore, points that would arise for consideration are:
- 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:6439 i.
Whether I.A.no.1/2022 filed under Order XLI Rule 27 of CPC for additional evidence deserves to be allowed?
And if so, whether dismissal of claim petition against insurer and fastening liability on owner calls for modification?
ii. Whether apportionment of contributory negligence between rider of motorcycle and driver of Lorry, calls for interference?
iii. Whether claimants are entitled for enhancement of compensation?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
On perusal of impugned award, it is seen that only reason on which tribunal has exonerated insurer and held owner liable to pay compensation is that as on date of accident, insured vehicle (Lorry) was not issued with fitness certificate.
Accident occurred on 22.06.2020.
Existence of fitness certificate would go to root of matter insofar as liability of insurer.
Hence, it is held that I.A.no.1/2022 deserves to be allowed and dismissal of claim petition against insurer requires to be set-aside.

opennyai_summary.decision:
Taking note of period of inpatient treatment at 8 days and amount for which medical bills were produced, tribunal awarded Rs.1,11,730/-.
Same appears just and proper and therefore not interfered with.
Considering said period as lay- off, claimant would be entitled for Rs.41,250/-.
Further, taking note of number of fractures and disability assessed, award of Rs.10,000/- towards loss of amenities would be inadequate.
If same is enhanced to Rs.50,000/- it would be just and proper.
Thus, total compensation would be Rs.6,86,105/-.
Point no.(iii) in MVC.no.771/2020 is answered partly in affirmative.
MFA.no.200736/2022
is allowed in part.
Compensation is reassessed to Rs.8,42,500/-.
But claimant would be entitled to only 75% of same with interest at 6% per annum from date of claim petition till deposit.
ii. MFA.no.200894/2022 is allowed in part.
Claimant is held entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.6,86,105/- with interest at 6% per annum from date of claim petition till deposit.
iii. MFA.no.200077/2023 is allowed.

iv. MFA.no.202872/2022 is allowed, but amount in deposit is ordered to be transmitted to tribunal for payment to claimant or adjustment against liability of insurer.
v. Apportionment of negligence between rider of motorcycle would be at 25% and against driver of Lorry at 75%.
But insurer would be liable to pay entire compensation to claimant in - 20 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:6439 MFA.no.200894/2022 (MVC.no.771/2020) in first instance and thereafter recover 25% from rider/owner of motorcycle.
 vi. Insurer is held liable to pay  compensation to claimants in manner  indicated herein.
It is directed to deposit compensation before tribunal within period of six weeks from date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
vii. On deposit, 40% is ordered to be kept in fixed deposit and remaining 60% is ordered to be released to claimants on proper identification.
In view of disposal of main appeals, pending applications are disposed of as unnecessary.
